description:
Follow-up from op-fm5 (2026-08-11).

Every transfer-function block gates on

    (current_input * 1e9).round() - (previous_timestep_input * 1e9).round() != 0.0

and only records an increment when that fires. The guard was originally a PERFORMANCE guard: under the old design each input change pushed a response onto a growing vector, so suppressing tiny changes suppressed vector growth. After the O(1) rewrite an increment costs a couple of flops and no memory, so the guard buys nothing.

It was deliberately KEPT in 0.2.0 so the recurrence ignores exactly the same sub-nano changes the old code did, i.e. so the rewrite was a pure cost change. But it has a real downside worth revisiting on its own merits: because previous_timestep_input is only updated when the guard fires, an input that ramps by less than 1e-9 per step is ignored INDEFINITELY rather than accumulating -- the block sees a frozen input until the running difference happens to cross the threshold. For a slow drift that is a genuine (if small) modelling error, and it is the sort of thing a real-time twin running for a long time can hit.

PROPOSED: either drop the guard entirely (increments of zero are free and harmless), or keep it but make it compare against the last ACCEPTED input in a way that lets sub-threshold changes accumulate. Whichever is chosen, re-run the analytic-superposition verification tests in */stable_transfer_functions/recurrence_tests.rs, and note that changing this WILL change numerical output very slightly, unlike the 0.2.0 rewrite.

Low priority -- correctness nit, not a defect anyone has hit.
title: chem-eng: revisit the 9-decimal-place input-change guard now that it buys no performance

description:
The Edwards-O'Brien blowdown V&V test (tests/edwards_blowdown.rs) exposes an energy-conservation limitation in TampinesSteamArray::step(). During the violent subcooled->two-phase decompression the h-form energy equation loses ~10x more enthalpy than the reversible dh=dp/rho, so the bulk liquid drops to subcooled and only flashes near ambient instead of holding the ~350-380 psia (p_sat at T0~505K) flashing plateau. Measured GS-1 plateau ~17 psia vs experimental ~350-367 psia; GS-1 pressure RMSE vs digitised Data ~276 psia.

Root cause: step() runs the explicit rhoEqn continuity rho = rho_old - dt*div(phi), but correct_thermo then OVERWRITES rho with the EOS (p,h) density each inner correction. That breaks the discrete cancellation of the h*div(phi) term in d(rho h)/dt + div(phi h) = dp/dt, so enthalpy is not conserved through a fast density change. Reducing dt (30us->10us) does not fix the ratio; it is structural.

NOTE: this is the ACCURACY limitation only. The STABILITY question Ethan raised (explicit scheme cools empty pipe to ~1C and pressure rebounds past 0.42s) is CURED by our PIMPLE array: past 0.42s min T=358K, tail pressure rebound +0.9 psia, void stable 0.997 -- no artefact. See test doc comment for full V&V write-up.

Possible fixes to evaluate (need own V&V): (a) conservative (rho*e or rho*h) energy update using the continuity-consistent density rather than the EOS density in the ddt term; (b) an internal-energy (e) formulation; (c) sub-cycling the flash within the corrector. Do NOT loosen the test tolerance -- assertions there are sanity-only by design.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsiDesktop
notes.content: RESOLVED 2026-07-16. Fixed with two coupled thermodynamic corrections (no clamps): (1) conservative energy ddt using the CONTINUITY density rho_cont = rho_old - dt*div(phi) rebuilt from the final mass flux (new fvm::ddt_coeff_old), so (rho_cont-rho_old)/dt = -div(phi) exactly and the h*div(phi) term cancels term-for-term against div(phi h), restoring rho Dh/Dt = dp/dt -- this is approach (a) from the bead; (2) pressure-eqn compressibility psi = d(rho)/dp|_h (central finite-diff of the (p,h) flash at fixed enthalpy) replacing the frozen quality-weighted isothermal rho*kappa_T, which was ~100x too small in the two-phase dome and let the pressure overshoot through the plateau. Results: GS-1 flashing plateau 17 -> 393 psia (target ~350-367); RMSE vs Data 276 -> 60 psia; stable full 600 ms; no non-physical subcooling (void grows gradually, fluid holds near p_sat). All 915 lib tests still green. See collaboration/edwards_tampines_regen/debug_log.md and tests/edwards_blowdown.rs doc comment. Residual: plateau ~8% high + shallow late decline (HEM-closure accuracy, separate from the missing-plateau failure).

title: TampinesSteamArray energy over-cooling under fast flashing (Edwards blowdown plateau under-predicted)

description:
Found while wiring htgr_sim_v1's turbine to a real torque balance (op-eukg). TurbineVisualState has exactly two variants: SteamGenerator (spins, casing_temperature() returns None -> neutral grey) and SteamThermo (casing coloured by inlet steam temperature, rotor_angle() returns ZERO). A plant that knows BOTH -- which htgr_sim_v1 now does, it computes a shaft speed AND a live steam state -- has to give one up. htgr_sim_v1 chose rotation and lost the casing colour.

Suggested fix (maintainer's call, engine crate src/components/turbine.rs): either a third variant carrying (ThreePhaseElectricGeneratorTurbine, Turbine), or a builder-style .with_casing_temperature(T) override on TurbineVisual that the generator variant can use. The second is smaller and keeps the enum honest about what each PHYSICS source knows.

Also noted while there, lower priority: TurbineVisual defines the rotor phase as theta = omega(t) * t. That is the true accumulated angle only for constant omega; during a speed transient the drawn phase advances at omega + t*domega/dt, which over-states the rotation during a run-up. An app-owned accumulated-angle input (integrating omega) would be faithful; the current form is documented but not exact.
title: TurbineVisual: a state variant carrying BOTH a shaft speed and a steam state

description:
Found 2026-07-28 while porting to v2. v1's GUI does: clone CIETState early in the egui repaint, mutate a couple of control fields on the clone, then overwrite_state(clone) at the end -- a full-struct store from a stale snapshot, ~20x/second. Sites: examples/ciet_educational_simulator/ciet_simulator_v1/app/panels_and_pages/main_page.rs:109 and :1194, and the frequency-response block in app.rs.

Impact in v1: mild and self-healing. CIETState is a publication surface, not the solver's internal state -- the physics thread recomputes temperatures from its own tuas component objects each timestep, so clobbered OUTPUTS are restored within one step. That is presumably why this was never noticed.

Impact in v2: NOT benign. CIETState also carries the CONTROLS the solver reads each timestep (heater power, pump pressure, set points). With OPC-UA writes arriving from remote clients at arbitrary times, a client write landing between the GUI's clone and its store is silently discarded -- remote control would appear to randomly not take effect, and would be near-impossible to diagnose from the client side.

Fixed in v2 by writing only the specific fields the GUI actually changed, under a short write guard, instead of overwriting the whole struct (main_page.rs:134 and :1236).

Consequence for port equivalence (op-wqk.13.6): v1 and v2 will NOT agree step-for-step with a GUI running, because v1 discards updates and v2 does not. The comparison must therefore be run HEADLESS on both sides to be meaningful.

No fix proposed for v1 itself -- out of scope for the v2 request, and v1 is the maintainer-validated reference. Flagging for his decision.
title: v1 GUI clobbers shared state with a stale full-struct overwrite (lost-update race)
